journal.description: One row per journal. This is the main/master journal table and contains journal identity, access type, publication/lifecycle information, identifiers, journal metrics, and descriptive information. The primary key used for joins is journal_id. ALWAYS use journal_id when joining this table to tbl_ebm; do not use old_journal_id, old_jour_id, journal_id_dummy, or journal_id_jms for the current journal join. For journal identification, use title when the user provides or asks for the journal's full name. Use subtitle when the user refers to a journal by its short code/abbreviation such as CMC, COC, CDR, etc. Code/abbreviation values must be matched against subtitle according to the application's journal-code convention; do not substitute unrelated legacy identifier columns. For subscription vs Open Access questions, ALWAYS use jtype: O = Open Access and S = Subscription. Do not use journal_type or IsOpenAccess for this classification. This table does not directly contain the actual editor/person assignments. When the user asks who is an Editor-in-Chief, Regional Editor, Section Editor, or any other editor/role for a journal, join journal.journal_id to tbl_ebm.journal_id, then use tbl_ebm.role_id to join tbl_ebm_role.role_id and tbl_ebm.editor_id to join tbl_editors.editor_id. eic_detail and eic_detail_old are not the source for identifying the actual Editor-in-Chief.

joins.note: Verified — the correct journal join, in both directions. journal_id_jms on tbl_ebm is a DIFFERENT identifier from a separate external system and must never be used for this join, even though it currently holds matching values in this dataset.

tbl_ebm.description: One row represents one editor holding one editorial role for one journal. This is the central relationship/junction table connecting journals, editors, and editorial roles. ALWAYS use journal_id to join to journal.journal_id — NEVER journal_id_jms, which is a separate external-system identifier that only coincidentally matches journal_id in this dataset. ALWAYS use editor_id to join to tbl_editors.editor_id when editor/person information is requested. ALWAYS use role_id to join to tbl_ebm_role.role_id when the user mentions or asks about an editorial role — never filter directly on ebm_role_name, which is a denormalized text copy kept only for convenience and can be stale. Do not choose another ID simply because it appears to contain similar data: journal_id is the correct column to use for the journal join, editor_id is the correct column to use for the editor join, and role_id is the correct column to use for the role join. ebm_role_id is a duplicate of role_id and should not be preferred for joins. This table contains assignment-level information such as main_section, section, region, acceptance_date, resign_date, approval information, and ebm_status. ebm_status describes the status of the specific editor-role-journal assignment and is independent from tbl_editors.status. For current/active editor assignments, normally filter ebm_status = 'Active' unless the user explicitly asks about resigned, historical, or inactive assignments. Questions combining a journal, person/editor, and role should normally use this table as the join hub.

joins.note: Verified — the correct journal join. Do NOT substitute journal_id_jms here; it is a different identifier from a separate external system.

Verified — the correct role join. Do NOT filter on ebm_role_name directly; join here and filter/match on tbl_ebm_role.role or tbl_ebm_role.nicename instead. ebm_role_id on tbl_ebm duplicates role_id — either can be used, but role_id is the correct one to join on.

tbl_ebm_role.description: One row per defined editorial role. This is a role lookup/reference table, not a table containing individual editor assignments. The primary key used for joins is role_id. Use role_id to join tbl_ebm.role_id to this table whenever the user asks about an editorial role such as EIC, Co-EIC, Regional Editor, Section Editor, or another role. The role column contains the shorter/original role name, while nicename contains the more readable/full role name. When interpreting the user's role wording, match against role or nicename as appropriate. This table tells the system what a role means, but it does NOT identify which editor holds that role or which journal the role belongs to. To find the actual person or journal associated with a role, join this table to tbl_ebm using role_id, then use tbl_ebm.editor_id for the editor and tbl_ebm.journal_id for the journal. Do not use this table alone to answer questions asking who holds a role.

joins.note: Verified — the reverse direction of the role join declared on tbl_ebm.

tbl_editors.description: One row per editor/person. This table contains the editor's identity and profile information, including editor_id, first/middle/last name, academic degrees, professional titles, university/institute/department, expertise, country, contact information, and researcher identifiers such as ORCID, Scopus ID, and ResearcherID. The primary key used for joins is editor_id. ALWAYS use editor_id when joining editor information to tbl_ebm.editor_id. This table does NOT directly determine which journal or editorial role an editor has; those relationships are stored in tbl_ebm. Therefore, when the user asks which journals an editor works for, what role an editor holds, or any combination of editor + journal + role, use tbl_ebm as the relationship table and join through editor_id. The editor's status column describes the person's account status (A = Active, B = Blocked, D = Deleted) and is separate from tbl_ebm.ebm_status, which describes the status of a particular journal-role assignment. Do not treat editor status and assignment status as the same thing.

joins.note: Verified — the reverse direction of the editor join declared on tbl_ebm.
